title: Bounded-below derived unit detected on cohomology sheaves
statement: Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with sheaves of commutative rings on sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories with cohomology $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose module pullback $f^*$ is exact. Write $f^*=Lf^*$ for its termwise derived functor and $Rf_*$ for total right derived direct image, computed by K-injective resolutions, with their canonical derived adjunction unit $\eta:1\to Rf_*f^*$ and counit $\varepsilon:f^*Rf_*\to1$. Let $K\in D(R)$ satisfy $H^q(K)=0$ for all $q<a$ for some integer $a$. If $\eta_{H^q(K)[0]}:H^q(K)[0]\to Rf_*f^*(H^q(K)[0])$ is an isomorphism for every integer $q$, then $\eta_K:K\to Rf_*f^*K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, $F=f^*:D(R)\to D(\mathcal O)$ and $G=Rf_*$. The module categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], since the sites are small in the specified universe. Exactness of module pullback and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] give its termwise triangulated derived functor, which is the $F=Lf^*$ specified in the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^q(FM)\cong f^*H^q(M)$ naturally. Thus $F$ preserves every lower cohomological bound, including negative ones.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-pur-exact-derived-adjunction-bounds] to the exact module functor $f^*$, its termwise derived functor $F$ from step 1, and the given canonical adjunction $F\dashv G$. It gives $G(D(\mathcal O)^{\ge n})\subset D(R)^{\ge n}$ for every integer $n$. Consequently $T=GF$ also preserves every lower bound. In particular $F$, $G$ and $T$ restrict to the full bounded-below derived subcategories of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. This uses neither a finite cohomological dimension nor an upper bound on $K$.

source.place: Tag 0D7T, lemma-bounded-in-image-downstairs, upper-truncation reduction; derived.tex Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing (1)

proof.text: Equip $F$ with the shift comparison $\sigma$ of step 1, for which $(F,\sigma)$ is triangulated. Clause (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique], applied to the given canonical adjunction $F\dashv G$ with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ and to $e_1=\sigma$, equips $G$ with shift comparisons $e_2$ such that $(\sigma,e_2)$ is compatible with the unit and with the counit for every integer shift: $\eta_X[a]=e_{2,FX}\circ G(\sigma_{X,a})\circ\eta_{X[a]}$. By [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint], since $F$ is triangulated, $G$ is triangulated with this shift comparison $e_2$. Hence $T=GF$ is triangulated with the composite comparison $\zeta_X=e_{2,FX}\circ G(\sigma_{X,1})$, and the displayed identity for $a=1$ says exactly $\zeta_X\circ\eta_{X[1]}=\eta_X[1]$, i.e. $\eta:1\to T$ is compatible with the identity shift comparison of $1$ and with $\zeta$. No comparison of $\sigma$ with the shift comparison obtained from K-flat resolutions is needed, and the unit $\eta$ itself is not changed. By step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], the bounded-below subcategories are full triangulated subcategories preserved by $1$ and $T$, so these structures and the naturality of $\eta$ restrict to $D^+(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 0D7T, lemma-bounded-in-image-downstairs, final triangulated-subcategory argument; derived.tex Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-heart-test-bounded-below] with both abelian categories equal to $\mathcal A$, $\Phi=1$, $\Psi=T=Rf_*f^*$, the restricted canonical unit $\eta$, and $E=K$. Steps 1--3 give triangulatedness, the specified shift compatibility, and preservation of every lower bound; the identity functor has these properties immediately. The integer $a$ in the statement puts $K$ in $D^+(\mathcal A)$. For every $q$, the required component $\eta_{H^q(K)[0]}$ is invertible by the hypothesis of the item. The cited heart test therefore makes $\eta_K$ invertible in $D^+(\mathcal A)$, hence also in $D(R)$ under the full inclusion. Its proof is precisely the finite-upper-truncation and cohomology argument of Tag 0D7T, so no convergence or infinite-limit assertion is needed.
